continuity.arc: Ambarisha’s devotion receives Sudarshana’s protection; a fasting-time dilemma leads to Durvasa’s pursuit and his return to seek the king’s forgiveness; Ambarisha responds with compassion and hospitality.
continuity.style: Traditional matte South Indian temple mural with firm dark contours, broad mineral-pigment fields, shallow space, restrained facial modelling, painted ochre ornaments, warm cream and muted foliage. The supplied photos guide story/composition only.
continuity.production: Native landscape-only candidate batch of ten stanzas; portraits are paused. All artwork remains unapproved.
continuity.anatomy: Ordinary humanlike cast uses one head, two attached arms/hands and two attached legs/feet, natural proportions and distinct faces. Deity forms are intentional only where specified in a scene contract; no unrelated identity or feather cue transfers between deities.
continuity.reference_mapping: Stanzas 1–9 map to numbered source photos 001–009; stanza 9 also retains source photo 010 as an explicitly duplicate #9 composition reference. Stanza 10 maps to source photo 011. Photos 012–017 are preserved as uncaptained documentary extras and are not attributed to stanzas.

plan_revision_history.reason: Stanza 1 showed unplanned repeated background worshippers; stanza 3 included Bhagwan as a worship object without its approved identity reference in the original call. The final plan constrains stanza 1’s cast and binds the Bhagwan forms in both scenes to the approved Guruvayurappan identity reference. Every candidate, including earlier versions, requires actual managed reinspection against this final plan.

scene_brief.source_summary: King Ambarisha’s mind remains absorbed in Bhagwan and the devotees despite his vast kingdom.
